docs.title: r503_uPython Documentation
docs.text: Comprehensive documentation for the R503 MicroPython driver (r503u.py) used with R503 fingerprint modules.

docs.title: What You Get
docs.text:
• API reference for every public method in R503.
  • Parameter and return value details in a standard documentation format.
  • Wiring diagram and electrical notes for MicroPython devices (for example ESP32).
  • Operation flow for enrollment and fingerprint matching.
  • GitHub Pages hosting guide.

docs.title: Quick Navigation
docs.text:
• Function Index
  • GitHub Pages Hosting Guide
  • Project README

docs.title: Fingerprint Enrollment
docs.text:
1. Capture image using get_image_ex().
  2. Convert image to a character file with img2tz().
  3. Repeat the capture/convert process for multiple samples (1 to 6).
  4. Merge samples with reg_model() to create a template.
  5. Save template into flash memory with store().

docs.title: Check Whether a Fingerprint Exists in Device Memory
docs.text:
1. Capture image using get_image_ex().
  2. Convert image to character data with img2tz().
  3. Search the library using search().
  4. Match result returns:
  5. 0 when a match is found.
  6. 9 when no match is found.
  7. Template number and match score in the returned tuple.

docs.title: Electrical and Pin Note
docs.text:
Warning

Some ESP32 pins are not usable as general GPIO even if they appear labeled as GPIO. For example GPIO 6 to 11 are connected to integrated SPI flash. See the ESP32 pinout reference before wiring.

docs.title: Hosting on GitHub Pages
docs.text: This project is set up to publish documentation generated by MkDocs.

docs.title: 1) Install Documentation Dependencies
docs.text:
Use your virtual environment, then install:

pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material pymdown-extensions

docs.title: 2) Preview Locally
docs.text:
From repository root:

mkdocs serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 to preview.

docs.title: 3) Build Static Site
docs.text:
mkdocs build

Generated output is in the site/ directory.

docs.title: 4) Publish to GitHub Pages
docs.text: You can publish in either of these ways.

docs.title: Option A: Automatic deployment via GitHub Actions (recommended)
docs.text:
This repository includes workflow: .github/workflows/docs-pages.yml.

  • Push to main.
  • GitHub Actions builds and deploys docs.
  • GitHub serves the generated site from the gh-pages branch.

If GitHub Pages is not already enabled:

  1. Open repository Settings.
  2. Open Pages.
  3. Set source to Deploy from a branch.
  4. Choose branch gh-pages and folder / (root).

docs.title: Option B: Manual deployment from local machine
docs.text:
mkdocs gh-deploy --clean

This builds and pushes to gh-pages.

docs.title: 5) Keep Docs Up to Date
docs.text:
• If API changes in r503u.py, regenerate function pages:
python tools/generate_function_docs.py
  • Review the generated markdown and refine examples/notes if needed.

docs.title: simplified_enroll
docs.text: Source: r503u.py (method R503.simplified_enroll)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Simplified enrollment of fingerprints. 1. Checks if fingerprint already exists in the device memory. 2. If exists returns 0 3. If not exists then it finds the next available location in the device memory. 4. Enrolls the fingerprint at the memory location where identified by the previous step.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text: simplified_enroll(num_of_fps=4, buff_no=1, timeout=20)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Default Description num_of_fps int 4 The number of times the finger has to be placed on the sensor. buff_no int 1 The buffer number where fingerprint stored timeout int 20 The timeout in seconds for each step of the enrollment process.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
• 0 on success (already exists or enrolled).
  • Otherwise confirmation/error code (for example 9 no match before enrollment path, 99 timeout/error).

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
1. Checks if fingerprint already exists in the device memory.
    1. If exists returns 0
    1. If not exists then it finds the next available location in the device memory.
    1. Enrolls the fingerprint at the memory location where identified by the previous step.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from r503u import R503

fp = R503()
result = fp.simplified_enroll()
print(result)
